title: FP8/INT8 perf metrics definitions (TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s + GPU util) — baseline vs canary
body:
Audience
- Runtime + SRE + Observability folks working on the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint and rollout canary.
- This doc defines the canonical metrics (counters/histograms), the exact timestamps used, and how we compare baseline vs canary without lying to ourselves.

Scope / non-goals
- Scope: online serving metrics emitted by runtime + scheduler, used in Grafana and perf-canary gating.
- Non-goal: microbench kernel timings (Nsight/NCU); those live in benchmark-lab artifacts.

Naming conventions
- Metric names below use the current internal convention: redwood.runtime.* for runtime and redwood.scheduler.* for scheduler.
- All latency metrics are in milliseconds unless specified.
- All token counts are integers. All rates are per-second unless specified.

Required dimensions (tags/labels)
These MUST be present for FP8/INT8 rollout and any perf canary evaluation.
- model_id: e.g., "llama-3.1-70b", "mixtral-8x7b" (exact names per model registry)
- model_version: semver or registry hash (pin for canary cohorts)
- region: e.g., "us-east", "eu-west"
- gpu_sku: e.g., "h100-sxm", "a100-80g", "l4"
- kernel_mode: one of ["baseline", "fp8", "int8"]
- kernel_variant: freeform string from kernel registry (e.g., "fp8_attn_v2", "int8_gemm_cutlass_3")
- scheduler_profile: e.g., "mixed_prefill_decode_v3" (or "default")
- deployment_mode: one of ["hosted", "dedicated", "private"] (hosted is primary for this sprint)
- cohort: one of ["baseline", "canary"] (perf-canary assigns cohort explicitly)
- request_type: one of ["chat", "completion", "embeddings", "rerank"] (for this sprint most dashboards filter to chat/completion)

Optional but strongly recommended dimensions
- route: API route name / internal route id
- customer_tier: e.g., "free", "pro", "enterprise" (hosted)
- streaming: "true" | "false"
- tool_calling: "true" | "false" (if we can tag reliably)

Core latency metrics

1) TTFT (time-to-first-token)
Definition
- TTFT measures: client-visible latency from request receipt to first streamed token emitted.
- If the response is non-streaming, TTFT is defined as time to first chunk produced internally (same event boundary as streaming would have used).
- TTFT includes: request parsing + queueing + scheduling wait + prefill compute up through the first decode step that yields a token.

Instrumentation
- Histogram: redwood.runtime.ttft_ms
- Start timestamp (t0): when request is accepted by the model worker (after auth/rate limit; "request admitted" event).
- End timestamp (t1): when the runtime writes the first token to the streaming buffer OR when the first token is available to the response writer.
- Observation: (t1 - t0) in ms

Notes / pitfalls
- For mixed prefill/decode scheduling, TTFT is sensitive to queue depth and batching window; this is expected.
- TTFT can improve while TPOT worsens (or vice versa). Do not gate on TTFT alone.
- TTFT should be analyzed separately for short vs long prompt regimes when possible; otherwise segment by prompt_tokens bucket.

Suggested breakdowns
- By prompt_tokens_bucket (e.g., 0–256, 256–1k, 1k–4k, 4k+)
- By concurrency bucket (if available) or queue depth percentiles (see scheduler metrics)

2) TPOT (time-per-output-token)
Definition
- TPOT measures: steady-state decode performance, normalized by number of output tokens produced.
- We compute TPOT at request granularity to avoid bias from partial streams.

Instrumentation
- Histogram: redwood.runtime.tpot_ms
- For each request:
  - decode_start (t2): timestamp when decode loop begins (after prefill is complete).
  - decode_end (t3): timestamp when the final token is produced (end-of-sequence OR max_tokens OR client stop).
  - output_tokens: number of tokens generated (excluding any special tokens not emitted).
  - TPOT = (t3 - t2) / max(output_tokens, 1)

Clarifications
- For streaming, we still compute at the end of the request.
- If output_tokens == 0 (early termination, error after prefill), we do not emit TPOT.

Notes / pitfalls
- TPOT is heavily affected by KV cache behavior and kernel selection for decode shapes.
- Tail TPOT (p95/p99) is the primary canary signal for customer-visible “slow generation” complaints.
- Very small output lengths (<16 tokens) can produce noisy TPOT; prefer filtering or reporting separately.

Throughput metrics

3) Tokens per second (tokens/s)
Definition
- tokens/s is primarily a fleet/worker throughput metric. We report two variants:
  A) request-level effective throughput (output tokens / total request wall time)
  B) worker-level aggregate throughput (sum output tokens / window)

3A) Request-level effective tokens/s
- Histogram: redwood.runtime.request_tokens_per_sec
- Per request:
  - wall_start (t0): request admitted
  - wall_end (t4): request completed (final byte written OR terminal status recorded)
  - output_tokens
  - request_tokens_per_sec = output_tokens / max((t4 - t0) seconds, 0.001)

3B) Worker-level tokens/s
- Counter: redwood.runtime.output_tokens_total (monotonic)
- Rate: tokens_per_sec = rate(redwood.runtime.output_tokens_total[1m])

Why we keep both
- Request-level captures user experience under queueing.
- Worker-level shows “raw capacity” and is less sensitive to individual request duration distributions.

GPU metrics (utilization, memory, clocks)

4) GPU utilization
Definition
- GPU utilization is sampled from device metrics (NVML/DCGM depending on environment) and attributed to a worker.

Instrumentation
- Gauge: redwood.runtime.gpu.utilization_pct (0–100)
- Collection interval: 5s (target). If 10s, note in dashboard.

Notes
- For MIG/partitioning, utilization may be “slice-level” rather than full device; tag with gpu_partition if available.
- Utilization alone is not a success metric. We care about tokens/s and tail latency; util is supporting evidence.

5) GPU memory
Instrumentation
- Gauge: redwood.runtime.gpu.mem_used_bytes
- Gauge: redwood.runtime.gpu.mem_total_bytes
- Derived: mem_used_pct = mem_used_bytes / mem_total_bytes

Notes
- Watch for FP8 paths changing KV cache packing; memory drops can be good but can also indicate disabled features or fallback modes.

6) GPU SM / TensorCore / memory bandwidth (optional)
- If available via DCGM:
  - Gauge: redwood.runtime.gpu.sm_active_pct
  - Gauge: redwood.runtime.gpu.dram_active_pct
- Use for diagnosing “kernel win didn’t show up end-to-end” cases.

Scheduler and queueing metrics (to interpret TTFT/TPOT)

7) Queue depth
- Histogram or gauge (implementation-dependent): redwood.scheduler.queue_depth
- Recommendation: emit per-worker queue depth as a gauge at 1s or 5s cadence.

8) Prefill vs decode time split
- Histograms:
  - redwood.scheduler.prefill_time_ms
  - redwood.scheduler.decode_time_ms
- These should be computed from scheduler spans (not kernel microtimings) so they reflect batching/wait.

9) Backpressure / throttling indicators
- Counter: redwood.scheduler.backpressure_events_total
- Counter: redwood.scheduler.admission_rejections_total (if any)
- These are used to interpret spikes in TTFT without a kernel regression.

Correctness and stability metrics

10) Error rate
- Counter: redwood.runtime.requests_total
- Counter: redwood.runtime.requests_failed_total
- Derived: error_rate = requests_failed_total / requests_total

Required tagging
- failure_type: e.g., "oom", "kernel_unsupported_fallback_failed", "timeout", "internal"

Canary guardrail
- Any increase in error_rate in canary vs baseline must be investigated even if latency improves.

11) Fallback / dispatch behavior
Definition
- For FP8/INT8 rollouts, the most common “invisible” failure mode is silently falling back to baseline kernels. We need to see it.

Instrumentation
- Counter: redwood.runtime.kernel_dispatch_total tagged by kernel_mode_selected and kernel_mode_requested
  - kernel_mode_requested: the mode intended by config/flag (fp8/int8/baseline)
  - kernel_mode_selected: what actually ran

Dashboard checks
- In canary, kernel_mode_selected should match requested for eligible shapes > 95% (threshold TBD by model).

Baseline vs canary comparison rules

Primary comparison approach
- Compare within the same (model_id, model_version, region, gpu_sku, request_type) slice.
- Baseline cohort uses kernel_mode=baseline.
- Canary cohort uses kernel_mode=fp8 or int8 (and must not be mixed inside the slice).

Aggregation
- Latency: report p50 and p95 for TTFT and TPOT; p99 is optional but often too noisy.
- Throughput: report median request_tokens_per_sec and worker-level tokens/s (rate over 1m).
- GPU metrics: median utilization and mem_used_pct over the window.

Minimum sample sizes (operational guidance)
- For canary gating decisions:
  - TTFT p95: minimum 500 requests per slice (or 30 min steady traffic, whichever is larger)
  - TPOT p95: minimum 300 requests with output_tokens >= 32
- If traffic is too low for a slice, do not gate on that slice; roll into a broader slice (e.g., drop customer_tier, keep model/gpu/region).

Noise handling
- Use a baseline window matched by time-of-day when possible.
- Prefer ratio comparisons: canary_p95 / baseline_p95.
- If the driver/CUDA/container changes, do not compare across the change boundary without re-baselining.

Recommended canary deltas (placeholders; final thresholds live in perf-canary profiles)
- TTFT p95 regression threshold: +5% sustained over 20 minutes OR +10% for 5 minutes
- TPOT p95 regression threshold: +3% sustained over 20 minutes OR +7% for 5 minutes
- Error rate threshold: +0.2% absolute (or 2x baseline, whichever larger)

How to interpret common scenarios

Scenario A: TTFT worse, TPOT better, tokens/s up
- Likely batching window/backpressure increased or prefill got slower while decode improved.
- Check scheduler.queue_depth and prefill_time_ms.
- Action: evaluate scheduler knob changes (batching window) and/or separate TTFT gating by prompt length.

Scenario B: TTFT better, TPOT worse, tokens/s flat
- Could be FP8 prefill win but decode path falling back or KV cache alignment issue.
- Check kernel_dispatch_total mismatch and KV cache related warnings.
- Action: inspect dispatch tags; capture nsys for a representative long decode.

Scenario C: Latency improved, error rate up
- Often indicates shape guardrails or kernel unsupported path causing failures.
- Check failure_type breakdown and kernel_mode_selected vs requested.
- Action: rollback canary for affected shapes/models; create targeted allowlist.

Dashboard query notes (Grafana)
- Always filter on cohort explicitly.
- Always include kernel_mode in the legend for cohort comparisons.
- Avoid mixing streaming and non-streaming unless the panel explicitly uses TTFT and TPOT definitions above.

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm whether embeddings/rerank routes emit equivalent TTFT/TPOT metrics or separate ones.
- Decide final prompt_tokens_bucket boundaries based on benchmark suite v3 distributions.
- Ensure MIG tagging is consistent across H100/A100 clusters (infra follow-up).

Changelog
- 2026-02-08: initial draft definitions from perf-canary needs.
- 2026-02-15: added kernel dispatch/fallback metrics; aligned with runtime metric tagging PR.
- 2026-02-24: clarified request-level tokens/s definition; added minimum sample size guidance.
